The study includes 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients using consensus criteria and describes behavioral features consistent with bvFTD (satisfies I4) and meets the patient sample size requirement (I5). However, it does not clearly meet I3 because imaging is described as SPECT and PET but not explicitly as FDG-PET. Crucially, the paper does not report any between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) (I6 not met), nor does it report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or coordinates (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are clearly triggered. Given missing whole-brain coordinate/voxelwise between-group results and incomplete full text, the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none.
(b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (patient group N=8, >=6).
(c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is diffeomorphic morphometry on structural MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I4 (participants are described as FTD but not specified as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls reported), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group versus controls). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the review’s key inclusion requirements and is excluded.

This VBM study includes a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) group (30 FTD patients meeting Neary criteria, i.e., behavioral-variant FTD), uses voxel-based morphometry, has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=30; controls n=20), and reports whole-brain voxelwise coordinates for subgroup analyses (e.g., FTD-specific voxels). However, it does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast that directly compares the bvFTD/FTD group to healthy controls (or reports such a contrast in standard stereotactic space) where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other diagnostic groups. Inclusion criterion I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. Therefore, although several inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I7, I8), the study fails to meet all required criteria and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD/FTD — paper specifies behavioural/frontal variant FTD), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6: 12 each), I7 (reports at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result comparing FTD to controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study uses tensor-based morphometry (TBM) derived from structural MRI, which is not among the accepted modalities of VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and I6 (the provided full text does not report results with explicit coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) in the excerpt; no coordinate table is presented). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded on the basis of failing required inclusion criteria I3 (and I6).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. It used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample (I4), had adequate group sizes (≥6 patients and controls) (I5), and reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level VBM results (I7) with results described in the text/figures (I8). However, the voxelwise contrasts reported are for PGRN(+) and PGRN(−) genetic/pathological groups (each containing a mix of clinical syndromes, though predominantly bvFTD) and the paper does not present a between-group contrast that isolates a bvFTD-only patient group versus controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis requirement that bvFTD-specific voxelwise contrasts vs. controls be reported.

The study uses FDG-PET (meets I3), includes pathologically confirmed FTD cases including Pick's disease cases (meets I4) and has sufficient sample sizes (14 FTD patients; 33 controls) meeting I5. However, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD (or Pick's) patient group to controls. Results are presented as diagnostic accuracy, regional ratings, and individual SSP/statistical maps, not as group-level voxelwise coordinate tables or contrasts. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used whole-brain voxelwise structural MRI analysis equivalent to VBM/SMP-based gray-matter voxelwise analysis) and I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise atrophy results) and I8 (results reported in figures and tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as a mixed FTD-spectrum sample; the paper does not specify a clinically defined behavioral-variant FTD [bvFTD] group nor isolate Pick disease patients as the target clinical group), I5 (patient imaging subgroups are smaller than required: tau-positive n=5, tau-negative n=4, fv-AD n=3 — all <6), and I6 (no between-group contrast is reported that specifically compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls without pooling with other patient groups). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered. Because several required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6) are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study uses volumetric MRI segmentation (T1/T2/proton-density) and lobar/regional volume analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (so I3 not met). It reports lobar/regional volume statistics (ROI-style) and no voxelwise whole-brain, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinate results comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails key whole-brain/voxelwise and modality inclusion requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed FTD per Neary criteria, corresponding to bvFTD) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only regional/ROI analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (contains intro, methods, results, discussion). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because it does not use an eligible imaging modality (I3) and does not report whole-brain voxelwise/stereotactic results (I6, I7); additionally the analyses are ROI/lobar based (E6).

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise atrophy results for an FTLD patient group versus controls; sample sizes meet the minimum (FTLD N=18, controls N=40). However, the report does not specify that the FTLD sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease (I4 not satisfied). The provided content is only the abstract/metadata and the full article PDF is not available here, so I cannot verify whether bvFTD-specific diagnostic criteria or MNI/Talairach coordinate tables for comparisons are reported (fulltext_incomplete=true). Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I4 (and inability to confirm I6). Exclusion criteria: none met.

This is an empirical multicenter FDG-PET study that includes a large frontal-variant FTD group (n=98) consistent with behavioral-variant FTD. Images were processed with voxel-based, whole-brain analyses normalized to the Talairach atlas and compared voxel-by-voxel to a normative database (Z-score maps, 3D-SSP figures). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for the FTD (frontal-variant) group versus controls are reported and used to derive disease-specific patterns; FTD results are not pooled with other patient groups. There are concurrent healthy controls (n=110). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore the study meets imaging modality (FDG-PET), clinical sample (frontal/bvFTD), sample size, voxelwise whole-brain reporting in stereotaxic space, and acceptable reporting locations (figures/text). Full text appears complete.

This is an exclusion because the neuroimaging methods do not meet the review’s imaging inclusion criteria. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study uses ROI-based structural MRI volumetry (SABRE regional parenchymal volumes and multivariate PLS) and does not report voxelwise, whole-brain coordinate results in MNI/Talairach space. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — the sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral/FTD subgroup, which corresponds to bvFTD), and I5 — adequate sample sizes (FTD subgroup n=8; scanning comparison group n=10; behavioral comparison group n=16). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 — imaging modality is structural ROI volumetry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET; I6 — no between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic coordinate space for the bvFTD group alone; I7 — no voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results in defined stochastic space. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used VBM (meets I3) and included a sufficient sample size (62 patients, 14 controls; meets I5) and included clinically characterized behavioral-presentation FTD patients (48 behavioral cases; meets I4). However, the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD/behavioral-only group versus controls in stereotactic coordinates — the between-group analyses presented compare the entire FTD cohort (behavioral + aphasic) to controls and the VBM correlations are within the pooled FTD group. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete for assessment.

This article reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and clearly includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bv-FTD) group (n=51) and age-matched healthy controls (n=14). The paper describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t tests comparing each patient group (including bv-FTD) to controls, reports significant clusters/brain areas associated with VBM contrasts and component scores, and references coordinate tables/figures (Table e-1 and supplementary material). Thus it satisfies I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes ≥6), I6 (between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), and I8 (results presented in tables/figures/supplement). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study used whole-brain VBM (I3) and explicitly reports analyses restricted to clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=7 PGRN bvFTD and n=11 MAPT bvFTD), meeting the bvFTD sample requirement (I4) and the minimum group sizes (I5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) comparisons and clearly identifies results coming from the bvFTD subgroup (I7). Results are presented in figures and supplementary material (figure e-1, table e-1), satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I8); the VBM workflow (SPM2/custom templates) and referenced supplementary tables imply standard stereotactic reporting of between-group contrasts (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no prohibited modalities, and bvFTD subgroup analyses isolate target diagnosis). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This autopsy-confirmed VBM study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons to controls (figures and text with corrected voxelwise results). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (bvFTD subgroup n=15 and n=30; controls n=35). Analyses include bvFTD-only comparisons and whole-brain voxelwise results across disease-severity groupings, satisfying the review’s target-sample and whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (FDG‑PET used), I4 (includes frontal variant frontotemporal dementia patients—fv‑FTD, equivalent to bvFTD), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6 participants), I7 (reports group‑level, whole‑brain voxelwise correlations within the fv‑FTD sample using SPM with Talairach localization). Not met: I6 — the paper does not report a between‑group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD/fv‑FTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space; the imaging results are within‑group correlations between fluency scores and FDG uptake rather than a patient>control whole‑brain group contrast. No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging and whole-brain analysis inclusion criteria. Exclusion criterion E6 applies: the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses of subcortical structures (striatum and thalamus) derived from structural MRI and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criterion I3 is not met (imaging modality is ROI structural MRI volumetry, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion criterion I4 is not met because the sample is described as ‘FTD’ without specification that participants were clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criterion I6 and I7 are not met because no between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space or whole-brain voxelwise results are reported. Inclusion criterion I5 (N>=6 patient group) is met (21 patients). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The full text reports an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=66) with healthy controls (n=30). Whole-brain voxel-wise VBM comparisons of bvFTD subgroups versus controls are described (FWE-corrected results, direct subtype comparisons, figures and voxelwise analyses). The study therefore meets imaging modality (I3: VBM), sample criteria (I4: clinically diagnosed bvFTD), sample size (I5: ≥6 patients and controls), between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic space (I6), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (I7,I8). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: none.

Study uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) normalized to an MNI template and reports group-level voxelwise contrasts. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=12) and a healthy control group (n=30), meeting minimum sample size requirements. The paper presents whole-brain VBM results comparing the bvFTD group to controls (figures and text) and direct group contrasts; methods state normalization to the standard MNI template, indicating results are in a defined stereotactic space. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, reviews, confounded samples) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses VBM and reports whole-brain, group-level VBM contrasts for clinical subgroups including bvFTD; however the bvFTD subgroup contains only 3 participants (methods report 3 bvFTD cases), which fails the minimum sample size requirement (I5: at least 6 patients). Controls are adequate (n=20) and subgroup-specific voxelwise results are reported, but the patient group size is too small to meet inclusion. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and result-reporting inclusion criteria. It uses volumetric MRI whole-brain and ventricular atrophy measures (BBSI/VBSI), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 and I7 not met); analyses are global volumetric comparisons and sample-size estimations. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD patients included) and I5 (≥6 patients and controls). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported; results are not in a voxelwise stereotactic space). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

The study meets the inclusion criteria for the review (resting-state fMRI was used; clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients were included; patient and control groups each have ≥6 participants; the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts with peak coordinates and whole-brain, group-level results). However, the sample includes comorbid neurological disease: three bvFTD patients had comorbid motor neuron disease. This constitutes concurrent neurological symptoms in the patient sample and therefore violates exclusion criterion E7. No other exclusion criteria were met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because E7 is satisfied, the study must be excluded per the review’s exclusion rules.

This study used FDG-PET and voxelwise SPM5 analyses in MNI space, reporting whole-brain group contrasts of the FTD patient group versus controls (satisfies I3, I6, I7, I8) and includes ≥6 patients (7 FTD) and ≥6 controls (18) (satisfies I5). However, the paper reports a generic 'FTD' group without explicitly stating that these participants were clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease, so it does not meet the required sample criterion I4. Because I4 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although the study uses voxel-based morphometry (I3) and includes some clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases within the sample (I4), it does not present any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). The paper reports VBM results for pathologic FTLD-TDP subtypes (type 1, 2, 3) rather than for a bvFTD clinical group, and the bvFTD cases are pooled within subtype groups. The bvFTD-specific sample size is not defined and likely below the required threshold (I5 not met). Additionally, the study allowed comorbid Alzheimer disease–related and Lewy body pathologies in participants, which conflicts with exclusion criterion E7. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used VBM), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients: 19 bvFTD cases), I5 (patient group size >=6; control group n=22). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 and I7 — the paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD (fvFTLD) group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space; analyses presented are within-group VBM regressions (combined FTLD and subgroup regressions) and direct contrasts between tvFTLD and fvFTLD, but no bvFTD vs control whole-brain voxelwise group-level results or coordinate tables for such contrasts. No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails to meet I6 and I7.

The study used whole-brain VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=10) within the FTLD sample (I4) with an adequate patient and control sample size (patients n=30 combined, bvFTD n=10; controls n=20) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5). However, the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group (not pooled) to healthy controls in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) — the between-group contrast reported is FTLD (combined) vs controls, and subgroup analyses report within-group correlates but no bvFTD vs control coordinate table or explicit between-group map (I6 not met). Consequently, there is no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result that is explicitly attributed to the bvFTD group for inclusion in a bvFTD-specific meta-analysis (I7 not met). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet all required inclusion criteria.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain/coordinate reporting requirements. It uses manual ROI-based structural MRI morphometry of the hypothalamus rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or provide results in standard stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach), so I6 and I7 are not met. This is therefore an ROI-only analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E6. It does satisfy clinical sample criteria (I4: clinically diagnosed bvFTD) and sample size criteria (I5: 18 patients, 16 controls). Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason: E6 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results).

This study uses FDG-PET and includes an FTLD patient group (N=14) and controls (N=13), but it does not specifically state that the FTLD patients are diagnosed as behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; it reports patients as ‘FTLD’ diagnosed per Neary criteria. The paper focuses on SVM multivariate classification and ROI/whole-brain weight maps but does not present a standard group-level, voxelwise between-group contrast in stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Therefore it meets I3 (FDG-PET modality) and I5 (sufficient group sizes) but fails I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s sample not specified), I6 (no reported between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach for the target group), and I7 (no clear whole-brain voxelwise group result identified for bvFTD). No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly met. Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study uses whole-brain VBM (I3) on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts with peak coordinates (I6, I7, I8). However, patient group sizes for the reported bvFTD subgroup contrasts are n=5 for each pathology (PiD, CBD, FTLD-TDP type 1), which fails the sample size requirement of at least 6 participants per patient group (I5). Although the total bvFTD sample is 15, the paper does not report a pooled bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast with >=6 subjects per group; all reported group-level whole-brain results are for subgroups of 5. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study must be excluded due to failing I5 (insufficient per-group sample size).

The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and included an FTD group meeting Neary criteria with behavioral features consistent with bvFTD (I4). Imaging sample sizes meet thresholds in the VBM subset (6 FTD, 13 controls), satisfying I5. However, the VBM analysis was a covariate-only regression collapsed across groups; the paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to controls nor any whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Inclusion met: I5 (patient group sizes: MAPT n=12, GRN n=8). Inclusion not met: I3 — imaging modality is structural MRI volumetry (boundary-shift integral and Freesurfer hippocampal volumes), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I4 — sample comprises genetically defined FTD (MAPT/GRN) not explicitly clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or PPA/Pick’s disease as required; I6/I7 — no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results reported in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables/figures comparing a bvFTD group to controls. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were directly applicable. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore study is excluded.

This is an empirical study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13) and age-matched healthy controls (n=25). The paper uses VBM (in addition to DTI/TBSS) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) with results presented in MNI standard space (TBSS and VBM analyses described and displayed). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6) for patient and control groups. The bvFTD group is reported separately (not pooled with other patient groups). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables, references) is present. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because its imaging analysis is cortical thickness (surface-based volumetric MRI/cortical thickness) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, thus meeting exclusion criterion E9. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present), I5 (patient and control sample sizes ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise cortical-thickness results), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures as described). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality requirement: VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET) and I6 (no clear reporting of between-group results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] within the provided full text/tables). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis based on E9 (and I3/I6 not met).

Full text provided is only an abstract; core methods and results sections not available. From the abstract we can confirm: I3 (VBM used) and I4 (bvFTD sample present). We cannot verify I5 (sample sizes not reported), I6 (no explicit report of between-group contrast coordinates in MNI or Talairach comparing bvFTD vs controls), or I7 (unable to confirm reporting of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates). No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Because essential inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending full text access.

This is an empirical VBM study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons involving bvFTD groups and healthy controls. The methods describe voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with generalized linear models and permutation-derived FWE thresholds; results report group-level, whole-brain contrasts (bvFTD C9+ vs controls; bvFTD noncarriers vs controls) and interaction effects, with coordinates/results referenced in table e-3 and figure 3. The bvFTD patient groups meet the sample size threshold (C9+ bvFTD n=15; bvFTD noncarriers n=48) and healthy controls are included. Whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample and reported in text/figures/tables (supplement). Therefore the paper satisfies imaging modality (I3), bvFTD sample (I4), sample size (I5), between-group contrasts in stereotactic space with bvFTD not pooled (I6), whole-brain group-level voxelwise evidence (I7), and allowance for results in supplements/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=15) and healthy controls (n=18). The paper uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) registered to MNI space and reports voxelwise, group-level between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs controls) with family-wise error correction and cluster/TFCE results; figures and text describe results overlaid on the MNI standard brain. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (VBM modality; clinical bvFTD sample; sample sizes ≥6 for patient and control groups; between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space; whole-brain voxelwise group-level results; reporting in figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no concurrent psychiatric/other dementia in sample, not a methods-only paper, and not limited to seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This task-based fMRI study examines clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients (Neary criteria, n=20) versus healthy controls (n=18) and reports whole-brain, voxel-wise group contrasts. Imaging modality: task fMRI with voxel-wise grey-matter correction (meets I3). Sample includes bvFTD patients (meets I4) with >=6 participants per group (meets I5). The paper reports between-group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (Talairach/MNI coordinates presented and thresholded whole-brain; meets I6) and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (meets I7). Coordinates and results are reported in tables/figures/text (meets I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Although this study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=11) and healthy controls (n=20) and uses [18F]-FDG-PET with voxelwise SPM analyses (satisfying I3, I4, I5), it does NOT report a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs controls) in standard stereotactic space. The imaging results reported are voxelwise regression correlations between deficit scores and metabolism across all subjects and cluster coordinates from those regressions (Table 2), not a group-level whole-brain bvFTD > control or control > bvFTD contrast. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. The full text appears complete (methods, results, figures, tables, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this study used voxel-based morphometry and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup with adequate sample size (12 bvFTD patients; 17 controls), it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The reported VBM analyses are regression associations of grey matter with flavour identification across the combined FTLD cohort, with mention that similar associations persisted in a bvFTD-restricted subgroup analysis (at a relaxed threshold) but no clear, reported whole-brain, between-group voxelwise results or coordinates for a bvFTD vs control contrast are provided. Therefore Inclusion Criteria I6 (between-group bvFTD vs control contrast) and I7 (clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified as coming from bvFTD group) are not satisfied, so the study must be excluded.

This study uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=12) (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes for patients and controls (bvFTD=12, controls=30) (I5). It reports between-group, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (ANCOVA, SPM8, DARTEL normalization to MNI space) comparing bvFTD to controls and to probable AD with voxelwise results and cluster-level FWE-corrected findings (satisfies I6 and I7). Whole-brain results are described in the text and supplementary materials (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical original data, not seed-only/DTI/thickness only). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the paper does not report any bvFTD-specific whole-brain (voxelwise) group contrast: analyses are reported for a pooled FTD sample (FTD n=52, comprising bvFTD=17, svPPA=18, nfvPPA=17) rather than for the behavioral-variant subgroup alone. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (bvFTD patients are included in the sample: bvFTD n=17), I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=17 and control group n=18, both >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD-only group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly labeled as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a resting-state fMRI study using graph-theoretical analysis on 90 AAL regions in 18 probable bvFTD patients and 50 controls, so imaging modality (I3), diagnostic sample (I4), and sample size requirements (I5) are satisfied. However the paper reports ROI/parcellation-based network metrics and region labels (AAL regions) rather than voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). No voxelwise coordinate tables or explicit whole-brain stereotactic contrasts are provided, so it does not meet I6 and I7. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=18). Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry analyses are reported, including between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD patients to controls (regions of decreased grey matter density in bvFTD are listed) and voxelwise regression results (threshold p<0.001, k=30). The methods specify use of SPM8/VBM, and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly described and referenced (with full-size tables/figures implied). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, and comorbid psychiatric/neurological exclusions were applied). Therefore the study meets the review’s imaging, sample size, bvFTD sample, and whole-brain result requirements.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically-diagnosed FTD patients including bvFTD cases (I4). The total patient sample is 15 (meets minimum N≥6) and 16 healthy controls were available (I5). However, the paper does not report a between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that compares the bvFTD subgroup alone to healthy controls (I6 not met). The reported whole-brain contrast appears to be for the combined FTD group versus controls and subsequent analyses are ROI-based; no group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample is provided (I7 not met). Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and bvFTD-specific whole-brain results are absent, the study is excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) with MRI controls, and reports between-group contrasts in MNI space. However, it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result that is clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone: bvFTD vs. controls results are reported as ROI / small-volume-corrected analyses, while whole-brain voxelwise results are only reported for the combined FTD group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I7. No formal exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the manuscript content, so exclusion is due to failure to meet all inclusion criteria (I7). Full text appears complete.

This study uses FDG-PET (met I3) and includes sufficient group sizes (9 carriers, 11 noncarriers; met I5). However, the participant group consists of GRN mutation carriers who are asymptomatic or clinically symptomatic no dementia, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease patients. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD/Pick patient sample), I6 (between-group contrast specifically comparing bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result coming from a bvFTD target sample) are not met. The paper does report whole-brain SPM contrasts, but these are for GRN mutation carriers versus noncarriers, not a bvFTD patient group. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Based on failure to meet the key diagnostic/sample-related inclusion criteria for this review, the study is excluded.

The full text reports an empirical study that used whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) with MNI registration and voxelwise analyses, including group comparisons and covariate analyses reported at the group level. The sample includes 22 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 35 controls (both >6). The paper reports between-group contrasts and voxelwise whole-brain results (with coordinates and figures) comparing bvFTD to controls and describes the frontal/temporal masks and significant clusters. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not FC/DTI/cortical thickness-only, and no indication of disqualifying comorbidities). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is INCLUDED.

The study reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses including VBM (grey matter VBM methods described) and DTI; it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort (n=27) and healthy controls (n=20) exceeding the minimum sample sizes; results are reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts projected to MNI space with FWE-corrected statistics and figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria for the review are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (study is empirical, not ROI-only, not a review, and includes VBM whole-brain results).

This is an empirical longitudinal imaging study that includes a separately reported bvFTD group (n=12) and healthy controls (n=15), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) alongside DTI, and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts registered to MNI space. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). VBM results are described and overlaid on the MNI standard brain, indicating whole-brain voxelwise findings for the bvFTD group vs controls. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, DTI-only, concurrent psychiatric/other dementia confounds) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This empirical study used resting-state fMRI and VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=15) (I4) and matched healthy controls (n=15), meeting the minimum sample-size requirement (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported: functional data were normalized to Talairach space and group contrasts versus controls are described (RS-fMRI network differences and VBM whole-brain clusters), satisfying the requirement for between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (I6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain results attributable to the bvFTD sample (I7), and results are presented in the main text/figures consistent with acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=25) and healthy controls (n=25) (meets I4 and I5). However, it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violates I3) and reports only region-based structural MRI volumetric/ROI analyses (FreeSurfer hippocampus, entorhinal, parahippocampal, composite MTL) rather than any whole-brain, voxelwise results in standard (MNI/Talairach) space and provides no coordinate tables or voxelwise contrasts (violates I6 and I7/I8). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). PiB PET was used only as a biomarker for diagnosis, not as a whole-brain FDG/PET/VBM-type analysis. Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Given these failures to meet required imaging and whole-brain/coordinate reporting criteria, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study uses VBM (and DTI) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=20) with healthy controls (N=31), and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results within the bvFTD group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample), and I8 (results reported in standard formats). However, the paper did not acquire imaging for control participants and did not report any between-group whole-brain contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no between-group coordinate-based contrast of bvFTD vs controls). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete. As I6 is not met, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I6 based on the provided full text. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM; FDG-PET was also performed), I4 (sample comprises clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), I5 (patient N=20; controls N=20), and I7 (reports at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample — the within-patient VBM regression reporting MNI coordinates for the IFG). Not met: I6 — although a two-sample VBM group comparison versus controls is described, the provided text does not report any between-group contrast result in a defined stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach) that would fulfill I6. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered by the provided content. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Because I6 is a required inclusion criterion and is not demonstrably satisfied in the provided content, the study must be excluded.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of T1-weighted MRI and structural covariance analysis (ICA) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts in MNI space. It includes 24 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and 30 controls (both >6), and reports group-level whole-brain results comparing bvFTD to controls/AD (e.g., decreased anterior cingulate network integrity in bvFTD, voxelwise atrophy in insula). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness–only, and no problematic comorbid-sample stated). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has adequate sample sizes (14 bvFTD, 12 controls) (I5). However, the analyses are ROI/graph-theory based (AAL parcellation and Network Centrality) and do not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI or Talairach space. Therefore it does not meet I6 or I7. Because it reports only ROI/region-based connectivity/graph metrics with no whole-brain voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion (E6) applied: this study performs atlas-based ROI volumetry of cerebellar subregions from T1-weighted MRI and reports region-wise volumes and Mann–Whitney tests, but does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise results or stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient groups and control group sizes meet the >=6 threshold: MAPT n=20, GRN n=7, C9orf72 n=17, controls n=18). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is volumetric T1 ROI analysis, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Excluded because exclusion criterion E7 is met: the patient sample includes concurrent neurological/psychiatric conditions (one patient with ALS, one with Paget’s disease, two with parkinsonian signs, one with psychotic symptoms), violating the requirement to exclude samples with concurrent neurological or psychiatric diagnoses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (use of VBM), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among the cohort), I5 (patient group n=10 and control group n=20, both ≥6), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group results for the studied patient group), I8 (results reported in figures/tables and text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — the paper does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls; the reported contrasts are for a genetically defined FTD/SQSTM1 carrier group (mixed phenotypes) rather than an isolated bvFTD group. Therefore it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for a bvFTD-specific meta-analysis.

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with results reported in MNI space and figures/tables, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=39) and healthy controls (n=61), and presents between-group voxelwise contrasts and brain–behavior correlations specifically for the bvFTD group versus controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (≥6). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). No exclusion criteria from the review were met (not a review/meta-analysis; not ROI-only; imaging modality includes VBM; patient sample appropriate).

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, uses whole-brain voxelwise longitudinal MRI morphometry (VBM-like) and meets sample-size requirements, the primary voxelwise analyses are reported on a combined FTLD group (bvFTD + svPPA). The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that isolates the bvFTD group versus controls (bvFTD is pooled with svPPA), so it fails to meet I6 and I7. Full text is complete.

Exclusion decision: No exclusion criteria from the review were met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (study used VBM) and I5 (patient groups and control groups each have ≥6 participants). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (the sample does NOT explicitly include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Pick’s disease — participants are grouped by primary post-mortem pathology subtypes, not by clinical bvFTD diagnosis), I6 (no between-group contrast is reported that specifically compares a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD target group). Therefore the study does not address the review’s target population (bvFTD/Pick’s) despite using VBM and adequate group sizes, so it must be excluded.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients in the imaging subset (bvFTD n=14) (I4), and meets minimum group sizes for patients and controls (imaged bvFTD n=14; controls n=27) (I5). However, the imaging analyses report voxelwise correlations of principal component scores across a transdiagnostic cohort and do not present any between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that compares a bvFTD group versus controls without pooling with other patient groups. Thus inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for bvFTD-focused VBM studies: it used voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=7) (I4) with sufficient sample size (≥6) and healthy controls (n=40) (I5), reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts versus controls with MNI coordinates illustrated in figures (I6,I7,I8). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and is sufficiently complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met (no review, not ROI-only, empirical VBM whole-brain results present, and imaging modality is acceptable).

This study uses resting-state fMRI and graph/network (ROI-based) analyses in a sample that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD (n=38) and healthy controls (n=32), but it does not report whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Instead, results are presented as network/ROI-based connectivity metrics (220-node parcellation) and network-based statistics (NBS). Therefore it fails the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain results. Exclusion ID E6 applies (only ROI/network analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (fMRI), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 and I7 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach; no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result identified). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses voxel‑based morphometry), I4 (clinical bvFTD sample), I5 (sufficient sample sizes: 25 bvFTD, 21 controls), I7 (reports group‑level whole‑brain voxelwise VBM results within the bvFTD sample), and I8 (results presented in tables/figures). However it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between‑group VBM (bvFTD vs controls) whole‑brain contrast in MNI/Talairach space. The imaging analysis consists of voxelwise multiple regressions within the bvFTD group correlating atrophy with behavioural valence scores, not a bvFTD > control or control > bvFTD group comparison. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study should be excluded.

The study uses whole-brain VBM and reports voxelwise group contrasts (I3, I7, I8) and has adequate sample sizes (I5). However, the symptomatic participants are described as genetic FTD mutation carriers and not explicitly as clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease; contrasts compare mutation carriers to noncarriers rather than a bvFTD group. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (bvFTD/Pick’s diagnosis) and I6 (a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls in stereotactic space) are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Hence the study is excluded from the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses VBM and resting-state fMRI (and DTI) (I3, I4) and sample sizes meet the minimum (I5). However, the full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls with coordinate tables or clearly-identified whole-brain voxelwise group-level results derived from the bvFTD sample. Thus inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. Full text appears complete and not truncated. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were violated.

This study used resting-state fMRI and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=50; controls n=32) (meets I3, I4, I5). However, the reported results are ROI/network-based (AAL nodes, seed-based connectivity, network-based statistics and graph metrics) and do not present whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables for bvFTD versus controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. It meets exclusion criteria E6 (reports ROI/network analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (reports seed-based functional connectivity/network analyses rather than voxelwise whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on voxelwise whole-brain contrasts with stereotactic coordinates.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that specifically recruited clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (probable and pathology-confirmed definite cases) and healthy controls, with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD and NL groups each >6).
